prerequisites: Competencies acquired in the Algorithms and Data Structures module
Competencies acquired in the Database Systems module

learning_outcomes.text: Students know challenges in building Distributed Systems.
Students know reactive, distributed programming (Actor Programming).
Students know techniques for digital representation and data serialization (Encoding).
Students know methods for the functioning of networks (Communication).
Students know standards for structuring and querying data (Data Models and Query Languages).
Students know algorithms and data structures for distributed data processing (Storage and Retrieval).
Students know techniques to ensure fault tolerance and availability (Replication and Partitioning).
Students know techniques to ensure consistency and agreement (Consistency and Consensus).
Students know algorithms for distributed transaction management (Transactions).
Students know frameworks for distributed batch processing of data-intensive tasks (Batch Processing).
Students know frameworks for distributed data stream processing (Stream Processing).
Students know the functioning of distributed database management systems (Distributed DBMSs).
Students know the basics of distributed query processing (Distributed Query Optimization).
Students are able to apply this knowledge practically in programming data-intensive, distributed algorithms.
Students are able to apply scientific working methods in independently identifying, formulating and solving problems.
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Actor-, Service-, Batch- and Stream-based distributed programming
Data structures for distributed data storage

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions to at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: To acquire credits, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution to at least two exercise assignments. Grading is from 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the B.Sc. Computer Science degree program.
